description: §12.4 — a single function whose body accesses BOTH a server-only resource (a ?{} SQL context) AND a client-only DOM global (`document.title`) is unplaceable: route analysis can assign it to neither side. It fires E-ROUTE-005 (error) — DISTINCT from E-ROUTE-002 (a server fn calling a separate client-only fn). Guards the S263-review hole where this shape silently shipped the DOM code into the server bundle.
rationale: §12.4: a single function accessing both a server-only resource and a client-only DOM global cannot be placed on either side (a server context has no `document`; a client context cannot reach the server-only resource). The compiler SHALL emit E-ROUTE-005 rather than silently place it server-side. It is NOT the E-ROUTE-002 cross-call shape, so E-ROUTE-002 does not fire. S478 (bootstrap triage C12): the `?{}` query is now handled and has a database scope. §19.8.3 (S451 R11): a `?{}` query is failable, so "outside a `!` function it must be handled at the site" (E-ERROR-002); §8.1.1: a `?{}` with no database scope (no `<program db=…>`) is E-SQL-004. The route shape under test is unchanged.
